text: Rust rejects two live mutable references to the same value so a mutable borrow stays exclusive: nothing else can read or write that value while it is being changed. That rule blocks data races and other memory-safety bugs from aliased mutation, including iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
thought:
Rust forbids overlapping mutable references to prevent data races. This prevents the bug class of concurrent modification.

It also prevents iterator invalidation and use-after-free bugs from aliased mutable access.

The restriction applies even in single-threaded code. Mutating a container while holding a reference to one of its elements can still invalidate that reference.
